title: perf-bench-scratch-harper-james-2026-03-22
content:
Goal:
- Quick smoke + sanity perf runs for Llama-2-13B quantized (q4f16) to validate latency/throughput targets for Dedicated pool 13B config. Check interactions between kv-cache hit rate and batching for short prompt workloads (chat-like).

Environment / Setup:
- Model: llama-2-13b-instruct (quant q4f16 snapshot v2026-03-20)
- Runtime: serving-runtime main@commit 8f3a2c (attention kernel opt + multi-gemm path)
- GPU: a100-40g (dedicated dev pool), CUDA 12.2, cuBLAS tuned
- Server: 1x worker, 8 intra-thread cores reserved, 32GB RAM free for KV cache
- Client harness: rps-bench v0.9 (python), 16 workers per client machine, results aggregated
- Prometheus scraping interval 5s, tracing disabled for these runs

Tests run (all runs repeated 3x, median reported):
1) Baseline (no kv-cache, batch_size=1, concurrency=1): short prompt (20 tokens in), gen 32 tokens
2) Batching sensitivity: batch_size=[1,4,8,16] with no kv-cache, concurrency scaled so total inflight = batch_size * clients ~ keep GPU saturated
3) KV cache hit test: prefix cache enabled with hit_rates [0%, 50%, 90%] for chat-turn repeats (prefix length 128 tokens cached)
4) Concurrency/throughput sweep: concurrency = [1,4,8,16,32] for typical chat seq len (prompt 30 in, gen 64) with caching enabled

Commands (harness snippets):
- baseline: python rps_bench.py --model llama-2-13b-q4f16 --batch 1 --concurrency 1 --prompt_len 20 --gen_len 32 --kv_cache false
- batch sweep: for b in 1 4 8 16; do python rps_bench.py --batch $b --concurrency $((32/$b)) ...; done
- kv hit: python rps_bench.py --kv_cache true --kv_hit_rate 0.9 --prefix_len 128 ...

Raw results (median of 3 runs) - Baseline:
- p50 latency: 95 ms
- p95 latency: 180 ms
- p99 latency: 320 ms
- tokens/sec (gen tokens): 420 tok/s
- requests/sec: ~13 req/s (32 tokens each)
- GPU util: 48%

Batching sensitivity (gen tokens/sec and p95 latency):
- batch=1: 420 tok/s, p95=180 ms
- batch=4: 1550 tok/s, p95=260 ms
- batch=8: 2800 tok/s, p95=480 ms
- batch=16: 3600 tok/s, p95=920 ms
Notes: batching gives good token/sec up to batch 8; beyond that latency degrades steeply (p95 jumps). For chat use-cases we should cap default batch to 4 or 8 depending on SLO.

KV-cache effect (prompt 30 -> gen 64):
- kv 0%: p50=220 ms, p95=420 ms, tok/s=380
- kv 50%: p50=120 ms, p95=260 ms, tok/s=820
- kv 90%: p50=90 ms, p95=160 ms, tok/s=1600
Interpretation: high kv hit drastically improves latency and throughput. For multi-turn chat, encouraging prefix reuse (or client-side caching) is critical for economics.

Concurrency sweep (with kv_hit ~80%):
- concurrency 1: p95=170 ms, requests/s=12, tok/s=380
- concurrency 4: p95=200 ms, requests/s=46, tok/s=1450
- concurrency 8: p95=260 ms, requests/s=84, tok/s=2600
- concurrency 16: p95=520 ms, requests/s=110, tok/s=4200 (note high p95 tail)
- concurrency 32: instability observed (queueing in runtime), p99 spikes >2s, not usable
Takeaway: keep concurrency per-worker <=8 to avoid p99 explosion. Autoscaler should prefer adding workers over pushing concurrency beyond 8 per worker.

Quick visual (ASCII) - batch vs tok/s:
batch | tok/s | p95
1     | 420   | 180
4     | 1550  | 260
8     | 2800  | 480
16    | 3600  | 920

Observations / Notes to self:
- Quant q4f16 on A100 seems fine for throughput but p99 still sensitive to long sequences + large batches (KV tile allocations?). Investigate allocator fragmentation.
- Kernel selection path picks grouped-gemm for batch>=8; seems faster for throughput but increases latency tail when mixed seq lengths present. Consider deterministic kernel fallback for low-latency tier.
- Tracing turned off; need a couple runs with tracing enabled to identify where p99 time is spent (attention vs copy). Schedule with Ethan.
- Memory: observed occasional OOM on batch=16 + concurrency>8; need to add guard in scheduler config and reject overly aggressive batching combos.
- Client-side suggestions: encourage shorter prefixes, provide SDK helper to do local prefix hashing + reuse.

Action items / next steps:
- [ ] Run 2 debug runs with tracing (low-sample) to profile p99 (assign Ethan).
- [ ] Re-run batch sweep with mixed sequence lengths to see variance impact (me).
- [ ] File Jira for allocator investigation if OOMs reproducible (JIRA-IR-3421 linked above).
- [ ] Propose default Dedicated pool config: batch_limit=8, concurrency_limit_per_worker=8, kv_cache_prefetch=true (draft in Confluence).
- [ ] Add a note in rollout checklist: when promoting q4 models, smoke-run these bench scripts against target hardware.

Random thoughts / gotchas:
- When running on H100 the p50 improves ~15-20% but p99 behavior similar; need to reproduce on H100 dev node next week.
- For fairness, also run on nvidia L4 (cost-optimized) to gauge tradeoffs; expected tok/s ~40-50% of A100 for 13B quant.

Appendix: useful logs/commands
- docker run --gpus=all ... rps-bench --model ... --out perf.log
- kubectl logs -f worker-0 | grep "inference_time" > worker0-times.log

End (scratch).
summary_notes: Short scratch: q4f16 13B on A100: batching helps up to 8, kv-cache huge win. Keep per-worker concurrency <=8. Follow-ups: tracing for p99, allocator OOM investigation, test H100 + L4.
